subject.title: fix(mcp): standalone apps stop hanging on stalled gateway requests

question: After the final MCP App operation waiter detaches, should an in-flight shared catalog refresh continue under the session runtime to warm cache, or should it be cancelled when it has no remaining consumers?
rationale: Both choices are technically viable but differ in resource retention, cache warmth, retry behavior, and stalled-server availability; the surrounding runtime is the contract owner, and the PR currently makes this choice across base and combined catalog paths.

options.title: Keep bounded cache warming
options.body: Retain the PR’s behavior so detached callers stop promptly while catalog refresh continues only until existing runtime disposal and MCP per-request timeouts.

options.title: Cancel orphaned refreshes
options.body: Abort the shared refresh when its final consumer detaches to minimize background work, accepting that later callers must start a new catalog load.

recommendation.title: Keep bounded cache warming
recommendation.body: Retain the PR’s behavior so detached callers stop promptly while catalog refresh continues only until existing runtime disposal and MCP per-request timeouts.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current proposed lifecycle and can provide the concrete runtime rationale, while a current-main MCP runtime owner should make the final decision.
